### Summary

When two HTTPProxies use the same JWKS server for JWT verification, Envoy may fetch the JWKS for one of them with the settings of the other. Contour treats JWKS URIs with the same host as the same server, even when other settings are different.

### Details

Contour configures Envoy with one connection for each JWKS host. If several HTTPProxies use the same JWKS host, this connection uses the JWKS settings of the `HTTPProxy` whose `spec.virtualhost.fqdn` comes first in alphabetical order. The other HTTPProxies fetch JWKS with these settings instead of their own. The affected settings are `validation`, the port in `uri`, and `dnsLookupFamily`. As a result, an `HTTPProxy` may fetch JWKS from a different port, or without the server certificate validation it has configured.

### Proof of concept

HTTPProxy `app` validates the JWKS server certificate against the CA certificate in `idp-ca` and the subject name `idp.example.com`:

```yaml
apiVersion: projectcontour.io/v1
kind: HTTPProxy
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  virtualhost:
    fqdn: app.example.com
    tls:
      secretName: app-tls
    jwtProviders:
    - name: idp
      default: true
      remoteJWKS:
        uri: https://idp.example.com/jwks.json
        validation:
          caSecret: idp-ca
          subjectName: idp.example.com
  routes:
  - services:
    - name: app
      port: 80
```

HTTPProxy `other` uses the same JWKS host without `validation`:

```yaml
apiVersion: projectcontour.io/v1
kind: HTTPProxy
metadata:
  name: other
  namespace: tenant-b
spec:
  virtualhost:
    fqdn: aaa.example.com
    tls:
      secretName: other-tls
    jwtProviders:
    - name: idp
      remoteJWKS:
        uri: https://idp.example.com/jwks.json
  routes:
  - services:
    - name: other
      port: 80
```

`aaa.example.com` comes first in alphabetical order. So `app` uses the settings of `other`, and the JWKS server certificate is no longer validated.

To list the JWKS URIs of all HTTPProxies:

```
kubectl get httpproxy -A -o custom-columns='NAMESPACE:.metadata.namespace,NAME:.metadata.name,FQDN:.spec.virtualhost.fqdn,JWKS:.spec.virtualhost.jwtProviders[*].remoteJWKS.uri'
```

If several HTTPProxies use the same JWKS host with different JWKS settings, they are affected.

### Impact

A user who can create an `HTTPProxy` can override the JWKS settings of other HTTPProxies that use the same JWKS host. This may allow making JWT verification fail, or turning off validation of the JWKS server certificate.
